observed: After seven strict checkpoints, the final snapshot passed 564/566 tests. The only failures were two new core optimisation postconditions, so the trajectory missed full-problem status by two tests.
Two checkpoint-1 null-validation defects persisted through checkpoint 5. Checkpoints 2–5 each passed their current tests in isolation, but the same inherited pair prevented strict solves five times.
The final snapshot passed every current core, functionality, and error test, but three inherited validation failures left it at 161/164 rather than strict.

Every checkpoint passed its core contract, but none passed in isolation or strictly. The final snapshot passed 58/89 tests; misses covered scheduling boundaries, glob semantics, validation, and inherited behavior.

The first three checkpoints were exact or near-exact. Multi-source joins at checkpoint 4 and versioning/resume at checkpoint 5 left the new feature nearly complete in isolation but preserved only 2/48 inherited tests at checkpoint 5; strict fell to 27/74.

Checkpoint 1 passed 30/30 after a timed-out attempt and retry. As stateful, C++/Rust, and advanced-window requirements accumulated, the final snapshot passed 92/172. The trajectory cost $19.04 and used 1,373 agent steps.

Checkpoint 7 was the run's only later strict pass after an earlier strict failure, but it is not evidence of full historical repair: checkpoints 6–8 set include_prior_tests=false, and checkpoint 7 had no regression bucket.
examples: checkpoint_metadata.csv records include_prior_tests=false for meshctl checkpoints 6–8
